plan.major: Sociology with a concentration in Criminology
plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-14 from the official Salem College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (current edition, catoid=34), Sociology Major with a concentration in Criminology (BA) program page (poid=935). Salem College publishes major requirements but no official semester sequence for this program (its Print Degree Planner is a blank worksheet), so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block. The full degree requirements, including the Salem Impact core (published separately in the same catalog), are not itemized here. Per-course credits are the Hour(s) values printed on each course's own official course detail page in the same catalog; the program page itself prints no per-course credits. Prerequisites naming courses outside this plan are disclosed in these notes and are not recorded as plan prerequisites. The introduction states the major requires eleven courses (33 hours, minimum): an eight-course core and three major electives, and that five of the eleven courses (15 of the 33 semester hours), including SSCI 395, must be taken at Salem. The recorded total (33) is the exact printed minimum: the Required core courses block (headed '24 semester hours') at 24 plus the three elective slots at the printed 9 semester hours. Prerequisites recorded only where every named course is a fixed course in this plan: SOCI 201 requires SOCI 100; SSCI 255 requires SSCI 130; CRST 150 requires SOCI 100 and one of CRST 100 or CRST 110 (its printed prerequisite reads 'SOCI 100 and (CRST 100/SOCI 270 or CRST 110)'; SOCI 270 is the printed cross-listing of CRST 100). CRST 100 is cross-listed with SOCI 270, as printed. SSCI 395's title is truncated as printed ('Interdisc Systems Think Capstone Project') on both the program page and its course detail page. This plan is the Criminology concentration only; the plain Sociology major is collected separately.

courses.title: Criminology Concentration Elective
courses.choice_note: Choose one of the concentration electives printed at a fixed 3 Hour(s): CRST 160 Juvenile Delinquency, CRST 170 Crime and Punishment, CRST 280 Criminal Law, or CRST 285 Criminal Procedure. The program requires three such electives (9 semester hours), recorded as three slots at 3 Hour(s) each. The printed elective list also names four variable-hour options, disclosed here and not listed on the slots because none is printed at a fixed 3 Hour(s): CRST 200 Independent Study in Criminal Studies (1-4 Hour(s)), CRST 220 Special Topics Criminal Studies (1-4 Hour(s)), CRST 270 Internship in Criminal Studies (1-4 Hour(s)) and CRST 290 Honors Independent Study Criminal Studies (3-4 Hour(s)); a completion using one of them above 3 hours totals more than the recorded total, as printed. Disclosed prerequisites of the listed options: CRST 160 requires SOCI 100 and CRST 100/SOCI 270 and CRST 110; CRST 170 requires CRST 100/SOCI 270 and CRST 110; CRST 280 and CRST 285 each require CRST 110 (SOCI 270 is the printed cross-listing of CRST 100).
